Loss of GCLC function in gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase deficiency leads to reduced gamma-glutamylcysteine and impaired glutathione biosynthesis, resulting in oxidative stress. This oxidative stress can disrupt general transcription regulation. partners.mechanism_chain: GCLC (HGNC:4134) —DISRUPTS→ gamma-glutamylcysteine (CHEBI:16900); gamma-glutamylcysteine (CHEBI:16900) —LEADS_TO→ Glutathione biosynthesis (GO:0006751); Glutathione biosynthesis (GO:0006751) —DECREASES→ Oxidative stress (HP:0002133); GSS (HGNC:4619) —DISRUPTS→ Glutathione (CHEBI:17697); Glutathione (CHEBI:17697) —LEADS_TO→ Glutathione biosynthesis (GO:0006751); Glutathione (CHEBI:17697) —DECREASES→ 5-Oxoprolinuria (HP:0002135); Glutathione biosynthesis (GO:0006751) —DECREASES→ Hemolytic anemia (HP:0001874). Loss-of-function mutations in GCLC (gamma-glutamylcysteine synthetase) impair the first committed step of glutathione synthesis, leading to reduced gamma-glutamylcysteine and subsequently reduced glutathione. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in GSS (glutathione synthetase) directly impair the final step of glutathione synthesis. Both deficiencies converge on the central pathway of glutathione biosynthesis, resulting in a critical depletion of glutathione. This depletion compromises the cellular antioxidant defense system, leading to increased oxidative stress and downstream phenotypic consequences such as hemolytic anemia. In the case of GSS deficiency, the accumulation of its substrate, 5-oxoproline, also leads to 5-oxoprolinuria.
